newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says cooperation among EMU "outs" voluntary.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says cooperation among EMU "outs" voluntary.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he was releasing a document from the European Monetary Institute, widely leaked to the press, which made clear that exchange rate cooperation among non-members of a single European currency would remain voluntary.
A letter he had written to the chairman of parliament's select committee on EU legislation on October 31 had given an accurate summary of the main points, he told parliament.

"The document gives opinions and advice on how, in the opinion of central bank governors, a so-called Mark 2 ERM for member states outside an economic and monetary union might operate in practice and how the monetary stability of the whole union might be safeguarded in future," Clarke said.
"It makes it quite clear...that membership and even cooperation on exchange rate matters will remain voluntary."
The EMI also said that such closer cooperation would be on a voluntary basis "at the initiative of the individual non-euro area member state," Clarke said.
"Unless we join stage three of EMU, we will retain, as now, control of domestic economic policy," Clarke said.
"There is no question of any fines or other sanctions being imposed upon us for running an excessive deficit."
